name: Lecture Teach-back (Feynman)
_note: Teach-back of the student's own lecture material. The case JSON carries the lecture material as ground truth. Standard metric keys re-pitched: medical_accuracy = content accuracy vs the material, clinical_reasoning slot = explanation structure & logic.

anchors.90-100: Clear, well-formed sentences throughout the explanation
anchors.70-80: Occasional minor errors; meaning always clear
anchors.30-40: Frequent errors; listener must work to follow

anchors.90-100: Explanations match the lecture material; mechanisms, terms, and facts are correct
anchors.70-80: Mostly accurate; minor imprecision on details
anchors.50-60: Core ideas right but several details wrong or muddled
anchors.30-40: Multiple conceptual errors against the material

anchors.90-100: Big picture first, then logically ordered steps; cause→effect chains explicit; good examples/analogies
anchors.70-80: Generally well ordered; occasional jumps the listener must bridge
anchors.50-60: Lists facts more than explaining; some logical steps missing
anchors.30-40: Disorganized; listener cannot reconstruct the concept

anchors.90-100: Flows naturally; defines or paraphrases jargon without being asked
anchors.70-80: Mostly fluent; explains terms when prompted
anchors.50-60: Frequent pauses; leans on jargon or reading-style delivery
anchors.30-40: Halting; cannot rephrase when the listener is confused

anchors.90-100: Checks the listener's understanding, responds to confusion gracefully, stays patient
anchors.70-80: Responds well to questions; generally engaged
anchors.50-60: Answers questions but never checks understanding

checklist.item: opened with the big picture before diving into details
explained the main concept(s) of the material in their own words, not by reciting
defined or paraphrased at least one technical term in plain English
used an example or analogy to illustrate a concept
answered at least one follow-up/'why' question correctly
re-explained a point more simply after the listener was confused
gave a closing summary of the whole topic
